name: Julia Thiele-Schuerhoff
current_role: Member of the Supervisory Board, Knorr-Bremse AG; Chair of the Executive Board, Knorr-Bremse Global Care e.V.
profile: German lawyer and heiress of Heinz Hermann Thiele (d. 2021), who built rail/truck braking maker Knorr-Bremse and held stakes in Vossloh and Lufthansa. She has sat on Knorr-Bremse's supervisory board since 2016 and leads the company-affiliated charity Knorr-Bremse Global Care.
interesting_fact: She cofounded Knorr-Bremse Global Care in 2005 after the Indian Ocean tsunami; it funds partner projects worldwide in education, emergency relief and water/sanitation/hygiene.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the board she worked inside the company as a lawyer: an LMU Munich law graduate, she was a Knorr-Bremse in-house legal adviser from 2002 to 2008. Before the 2018 Frankfurt IPO, she and her father were Knorr-Bremse's sole owners.
notes: The Thiele family has long avoided publicity. The best route is Knorr-Bremse corporate communications (those contacts are for journalists only), or via Knorr-Bremse Global Care.

name: Mette Brunsborg
current_role: Board member, Lars Larsen Group A/S (owner of JYSK) and Lars Larsens JYSK Fond
profile: Daughter of JYSK founder Lars Larsen (d. 2019). She and her brother Jacob Brunsborg (chairman) control Lars Larsen Group, the Silkeborg holding company that owns the JYSK home-furnishings chain plus BOLIA, ILVA, SOFACOMPANY and other investments. She joined the family foundation's board in 2019, taking her mother Kris Brunsborg's seat.
interesting_fact: When she joined the board of Lars Larsens JYSK Fond in 2019, she took the seat of her mother, Kris Brunsborg. The foundation's first gift under the new board was DKK 1m to Børns Vilkår to help children whose parents have mental illness.
deep_cut_fact: Away from the boardroom she runs her own farm (driver sit eget landbrug), according to the Danish encyclopedia Lex.
notes: Very private, with almost no public profile. Brother Jacob Brunsborg is the family's public face. In July 2026 Lars Larsen Group announced a new renewable-energy agreement, which could be an angle for an energy podcast. Best route is Lars Larsen Group press.

name: Wang Qicheng
current_role: Founder of the Hakim (Handing / 汉鼎) group; private investor based in Hangzhou
profile: Hangzhou entrepreneur born in the 1980s, who shares the Hurun listing with Wu Yan. While at Zhejiang University he founded Handing (Hakim) Information Technology, a smart-city systems integrator that listed on ChiNext in 2012. In 2019 he passed control of the listed company (later Haixia Innovation) to Pingtan state capital, and he now invests his own money across a portfolio of roughly 100 startups.
interesting_fact: He was an early backer of US EV maker Fisker, investing in 2017 for a stake of about 10%, and of Aurora Mobile (极光), which listed on Nasdaq in 2018. In 2020 he was named one of China's top five angel investors, the only one born in the 1980s.
deep_cut_fact: He started his company straight out of Zhejiang University's business administration department in 2003. When it listed on ChiNext nine years later, the 31-year-old was reported to be the youngest controlling shareholder of any A-share company at the time.
notes: Sources are mostly promotional Chinese articles, so verify before quoting. No personal channels are published. Hurun lists him together with Wu Yan. He has little English-language presence.

name: Jacques D'Amours
current_role: Co-founder and major shareholder (about 6%), Alimentation Couche-Tard; retired from the board in 2023
profile: Montreal-based co-founder of Alimentation Couche-Tard (Circle K), which started from one Quebec convenience store in 1980 and grew through acquisitions into a global chain of more than 17,000 stores. He worked at the company for 34 years, retiring as VP of administration in 2014, and left the board in 2023. He remains its second-largest shareholder.
interesting_fact: He was the youngest of Couche-Tard's four co-founders, alongside Alain Bouchard, Richard Fortin and Réal Plourde, and has been a billionaire since 2005.
deep_cut_fact: In the mid-1980s, aged about 28, he ran operations with Réal Plourde in Couche-Tard's small early office. The company's very first employee remembered him as 'more of an introvert' than his co-founders. His roles over the years included manager of technical services and VP of sales.
notes: Low-profile and retired from the company. Couche-Tard media relations may forward a request but does not represent him personally. Co-founder Alain Bouchard is the public face.

name: Anthony Langley
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Langley Holdings plc (Bergen Engines, Piller Power Systems, Marelli Motori, Clarke Chapman)
profile: Tony Langley founded Langley Holdings in 1975, aged 20, from the remains of his grandfather's failed engineering firm. He started by selling mining equipment to the UK coal industry, then built a group of 90+ subsidiaries through acquisitions such as Clarke Chapman (2000) and Bergen Engines (2021), both bought from Rolls-Royce. He is now repositioning the group as a supplier of grid-free, behind-the-meter power for AI data centers.
interesting_fact: Bergen Engines won its first independent power order for a new US AI data center in 2025: gas engines of 11.2MW each for E-Finity Distributed Generation. In May 2026 it won more than 500MW of orders from Liberty Energy. Langley says the group 'is now principally a power equipment supplier.'
deep_cut_fact: His Gladiator team won the 2024 Rolex TP52 World Championship in Newport, RI, the first British-flagged team to take that title and his first world title as an owner. Langley called tactics after handing the helm to two-time world champion Guillermo Parada so he could learn from him.
notes: A highly relevant guest for a data-center/energy podcast. He has given trade-press interviews (Capacity, June 2026) and attends Datacloud Global Congress in Cannes with his sons. LinkedIn is the company page, not a personal profile.

name: Stephen Lansdown
current_role: Owner, Bristol Sport (Bristol City FC, Bristol Bears, Bristol Flyers); private investor based in Guernsey
profile: Bristol-born accountant (b. 1952) who co-founded Hargreaves Lansdown with Peter Hargreaves in 1981. It grew into the UK's largest retail investment platform. He left its board in 2012 and moved to Guernsey in 2010, and now concentrates on Bristol Sport and private and impact investments. He co-founded the sustainable PE firm Earth Capital in 2008; it closed in 2024.
interesting_fact: Trained as an accountant, he started Hargreaves Lansdown trading from a bedroom in 1981. He later sold Hargreaves Lansdown shares to help fund Bristol City's redevelopment of Ashton Gate, and rescued Bristol Rugby (now Bristol Bears) when it was close to going under.
deep_cut_fact: He was an early convert to sustainable investing. In 2019 he said he had narrowed his focus to four themes: food security, energy security, clean water and waste management. Earth Capital scored every deal on its own 'Earth Dividend' ESG scorecard, mapped to the UN SDGs.
notes: He received a CBE in 2017. His energy-security and sustainability investing is a natural podcast angle. Bristol Sport is the most direct published route.

name: Susan Williams
current_role: Independent Director, W.W. Grainger (since 2020); President, Donald Slavik Family Foundation; Director, Mark IV Capital
profile: Susan Slavik Williams owns about 5% of industrial distributor W.W. Grainger and has sat on its board since April 2020, serving on the nominating and compensation committees. She has been a director of Newport Beach real-estate firm Mark IV Capital since 1989, and she leads the Donald Slavik Family Foundation, which focuses on wildlife and environmental education.
interesting_fact: As president of the Donald Slavik Family Foundation since 1995, she funds wildlife conservation in North America and Africa. She also sits on the board of the St. Louis Zoo.
deep_cut_fact: Before her board career she was a manager at Capgemini US. With her husband Felix she ran a custom home-electronics firm, The Screening Room, for about 10 years. She also founded Four Palms Ventures LLC.
notes: Low public profile. Grainger corporate communications or the investor-relations page is the only published route. The deep-cut details come from aggregator profiles (MarketScreener) plus Forbes; confirm them in Grainger's proxy before using.

name: Diane Goldman
current_role: Co-owner, Solil Management (Goldman family real estate, New York); philanthropist
profile: Diane Goldman Kemper (b. 1946) is a daughter of New York real-estate investor Sol Goldman (d. 1987) and one of four siblings who co-own Solil Management. Solil holds roughly 400 mostly Manhattan properties, including the land under Olympic Tower and the Cartier Building and part of the land under the World Trade Center. Her sister Jane runs day-to-day operations.
interesting_fact: Solil's portfolio includes the land under Olympic Tower and the Cartier Building, The Peninsula New York hotel, and about 17% of the land under the World Trade Center complex.
deep_cut_fact: She studied at C.W. Post College and the New York School of Interior Design, and once worked in the family company's residential leasing department. Columbia University has a 'Diane Goldman Kemper Family Professor of Epidemiology in Psychiatry' chair.
notes: Known publicly as Diane Goldman Kemper. The family is famously private (Forbes: 'doesn't want you to know who they are'), and there is ongoing family litigation over Solil, so avoid that topic. She has no published personal or office contact. The only published family entity address is the Lillian Goldman Charitable Trust (postal). Low relevance to an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Katarina Martinson
current_role: Chair, Indutrade AB; board member, L E Lundbergföretagen AB and other Lundberg group companies
profile: Swedish businesswoman (b. 1981) who, with her sister Louise Lindh, owns about 15% stakes in the family investment company L E Lundbergföretagen. Founded by her grandfather in 1944 and led by her father Fredrik Lundberg, it holds stakes in Holmen, Handelsbanken, Sandvik, Skanska, Indutrade and others. She chairs industrial group Indutrade and invests privately in brands such as NN07 and Lyko.
interesting_fact: When she became chair of Indutrade, she was the youngest chair of any company listed on the Stockholm Stock Exchange.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Norrköping, she grew up in Norrköping, Switzerland and Djursholm and is a Stockholm School of Economics graduate. In 2021 she was elected a member of IVA, the Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences.
notes: Fairly private. Lundbergs (whose holdings include Holmen, which owns forest and hydro/wind assets) and Indutrade are the routes. Her IVA membership suggests an interest in engineering and tech topics.

name: Sjamsul Nursalim
current_role: Founder/controlling family shareholder, Giti Tire / Gajah Tunggal group (Singapore-based)
profile: Indonesian tycoon (b. 1942, Lampung), the son of a rubber seller, who built a fortune in tires, property, coal and retail. His Singapore-headquartered Giti Tire sells in more than 130 countries. The family also holds stakes in retailer Mitra Adiperkasa (Zara and others in Indonesia) and Singapore-listed Tuan Sing Holdings.
interesting_fact: Giti co-developed the tires on BYD's Yangwang U9 Xtreme hypercar, which set a world speed record for mass-produced cars in September 2025. Brand Finance ranked Giti among the world's 10 most valuable tire brands in 2026.
notes: In his 80s and believed to live in Singapore. No death reports were found, but he has no recent public appearances. He has a long, sensitive legal history in Indonesia (the BLBI bank-bailout case), so avoid it. Forbes now lists him as 'former'. Day-to-day leadership of the businesses has passed to the next generation. Not a realistic podcast guest. The Giti contacts are generic corporate inboxes.

name: Samuel C. Johnson
profile: Samuel Curtis Johnson Jr. (1928-2004) was the fourth-generation leader of S.C. Johnson & Son in Racine, Wisconsin. He died on May 22, 2004 (listed on Forbes 1997 only).
notes: Deceased May 22, 2004 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Curtis_Johnson_Jr.). Identity inferred from the Forbes 1997 listing, which carries no source-of-wealth field. His daughter Winnie Johnson-Marquart (P03641) is in this lane, and his son Fisk Johnson now leads SC Johnson.

name: Zhao Weiguo
current_role: None. Former chairman of Tsinghua Unigroup; currently imprisoned in China
profile: A Tsinghua University alumnus who led chip conglomerate Tsinghua Unigroup and drove a major acquisition push in China's semiconductor industry in the 2010s. He lost control after Unigroup's 2021-22 restructuring, when his Jiankun group and Tsinghua Holdings exited. In May 2025 a Jilin court sentenced him to death with a two-year reprieve for embezzlement and related crimes.
notes: Not a viable outreach target: he is serving a suspended death sentence handed down at first instance on May 14, 2025 (https://www.caixinglobal.com/2025-05-15/former-tsinghua-unigroup-chairman-zhao-weiguo-receives-suspended-death-sentence-in-first-instance-for-embezzlement-of-particularly-huge-amounts-102319729.html). All his personal assets were ordered confiscated. Forbes lists him as 'former'.

name: Alexey Repik
current_role: Chairman, All-Russian public organisation 'Delovaya Rossiya' (Business Russia); founder of R-Pharm
profile: Moscow-born (1979) Higher School of Economics graduate who founded R-Pharm in 2001 with $40,000, half of it from his mother. It grew into one of Russia's largest drugmakers and state suppliers, and Mitsui bought 10% in 2017. In 2022 he stepped down as R-Pharm chairman and reportedly sold his R-Pharm assets. He chairs the business lobby Delovaya Rossiya.
interesting_fact: He started R-Pharm in 2001 with $40,000 in startup capital, half of which came from his mother. He had taken his first healthcare job in 1995, aged about 16.
deep_cut_fact: He funded construction of a large dog shelter in Yaroslavl, about 250 km from Moscow, designed to handle about 1,500 dogs a year.
notes: CAUTION: under UK sanctions since Feb 2023 and Canadian sanctions since May 2023 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aleksey_Repik). In 2024 he was an authorised representative of Putin's presidential campaign. Check the legal and reputational implications before any outreach. The only published route is Delovaya Rossiya.

name: Leng Youbin
current_role: Chairman and CEO, China Feihe Ltd. (HKEX: 6186); deputy to the National People's Congress
profile: Heilongjiang dairy entrepreneur who herded cows as a child and worked at a state-owned dairy farm for about a decade. He then took stakes in the farm and a dairy plant and built Feihe into one of China's largest infant-formula makers, with its own farms in northeast China. Feihe listed in Hong Kong in 2019.
interesting_fact: He earned his degree from Northeast Agricultural University by correspondence course in 1995 and later an EMBA from Peking University. At the 2025 Harvard China Forum he lectured on scientific cattle-raising.
deep_cut_fact: He calls himself a 'second-generation builder of the Great Northern Wilderness (北大荒)'. When the property boom tempted Feihe to diversify into real estate, he refused: 'If we had done real estate then, there would be no Feihe deeply rooted in its core business.'
notes: Active NPC deputy who speaks publicly on black-soil protection and on making dairy ingredients domestically. Contact would go through Feihe's investor relations; no published email was retrievable. Weak fit for an energy podcast, except possibly agriculture and energy angles.

name: Constantinos Martinos
current_role: Owner/principal, Thenamaris (Athens); the company is now run day to day by his son Nikolas
profile: Greek shipowner known as 'Dinos' (b. 1953, Glyfada). He co-founded Thenamaris in the early 1970s with his mother Athina, one of Greece's first female shipowners, and his brothers. After the brothers split off in 1990 and 1998 he kept Thenamaris, which now runs a fleet of about 90 tankers, bulkers, container ships and LNG carriers.
interesting_fact: He is a serious, low-profile art collector whose holdings include works by Picasso, Twombly, Basquiat and Warhol. Greek press dubbed him the 'invisible collector'.
deep_cut_fact: The Martinos family funded a new €10m building with 115 hospital beds at Asklipieio General Hospital in Voula, near Athens. In 2011 Lloyd's List ranked him No. 67 among the 100 most influential people in shipping.
notes: Very private. Son Nikolas Martinos runs Thenamaris, including an LNG-carrier arm (Thenamaris LNG), which could be an energy angle. The best route is Thenamaris corporate communications.
